newsitem.title: UK: Scots Nationalists back fight for devolution. [CORRECTED 08:05 03/8]
newsitem.headline: Scots Nationalists back fight for devolution. [CORRECTED 08:05 03/8]

text.p: Scottish Nationalists pledged on Saturday to campaign for a "yes" vote in a referendum to decide whether Scotland will have its own parliament again after nearly 300 years.
Activists at the Scottish National Party's national council (corrects name of gathering from "annual conference") voted overwhelmingly to back their leaders' decision to back a "yes" vote.
Earlier, their leader Alex Salmond told the 300 delegates the September 11 referendum was a great opportunity for Scotland.
"Scots want real change and a real parliament, he said.
The single-chamber parliament proposed by Britain's Labour government would take control of almost all Scotland's domestic affairs from January 1, 2000.
Britain's Conservative Party, which lost all its Scottish seats when it was ousted from power in an election in May, is the only party campaigning for a "no" vote in the referendum.
Opinion polls since the election show a majority of Scots, including about a quarter of Scottish Conservatives, want a separate parliament.
